newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pasminco leaving mine negotiations to Century.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pasminco leaving mine negotiations to Century.

text.p: Pasminco Ltd said on Thursday it would not enter negotiations with Aborigines on the future of its A$1 billion Century Zinc project but instead would let new subsidiary Century Zinc Ltd do all the talking.

"Pasminco is not entering negotiations with the Aborigines. The (current) negotiations will be conducted by Century Zinc," Pasminco's managing director and chief executive, David Stewart told a press conference here.
Earlier, Pasminco and RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd announced the sale of RTZ-CRA's Century zinc deposit to Pasminco for A$345 million.

Stewart was answering questions on whether the change of ownership of the Century Zinc project would have any affect on talks being held with local Aboriginal groups over the question of native title claims on the mine area.
Century Zinc's managing director Ian Williams said negotiations with local Aboriginal groups were still being conducted.
"It's a Century Zinc negotiation and I and my management team have expressed a desire to stick with the project," Williams said.

Stewart said if negotiations with Aboriginal groups were not eventually successful and the mine project did no go ahead, then Pasminco would apply the A$10 million deposit it had paid to developing the smaller Dugald River zinc deposit which had also been purchased in today's deal.
"I think the current negotiating process (on the Century Zinc mine) provides certainty. I'm confident the mine will go ahead," he said.
Williams said a further meeting with Aboriginal groups was scheduled for next Tuesday.
"We are making progress. We are cautiously optimistic and we aim to get a negotiated settlement within a month," he said.
The A$60 million aid package for local Aboriginal communities promised by the mine's former owners, was still in place, he said.
"As we go forward, people are becoming more comfortable but we'll have to keep pushing," Williams said.
